# CI Quality & Verification Checklist: HU-00-02 (CI Pipeline)

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review checklist to evaluate whether spec.md and plan.md define complete, unambiguous, and verifiable criteria for HU-00-02.
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command as a reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact.
**Review Ownership**: Mark an item `[x]` only when human review confirms the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied in the specification and plan.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` indicates that the requirement specification is complete, clear, and verifiable. It does not indicate that implementation is complete.

---

## 1. Execution Triggers & Scope

- [ ] CHK001 Are the specific events (pull requests and pushes to `main`) that trigger the CI pipeline explicitly defined in the requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the execution scope strictly bounded to the Sprint 1 repository without pulling dependencies from future sprints? [Scope, Spec §Requirements, Constitution Principio VI]

## 2. Mandatory Quality Gates

- [ ] CHK003 Are all mandatory verification gates (automated tests, static typing, formatting inspection, and coverage report) explicitly specified with strict pass/fail rules? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 Is code formatting explicitly specified to execute in read-only inspection mode (`check`) without modifying files in place during CI? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Constraints]

## 3. Failure Demonstration & AC-01 Verification

- [ ] CHK005 Is the non-zero exit code behavior for test suite failures explicitly specified as the gate signal to block integration? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-008, AC-01]
- [ ] CHK006 Are static type checking failure conditions and strict typing rules defined with unambiguous error reporting requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-008, AC-01]
- [ ] CHK007 Are negative failure scenarios (simulated test failure, typing mismatch, format violation) explicitly documented to prove pipeline blocking? [Verifiability, Spec §User Story 1, Quickstart §3]

## 4. Multiplatform Parity & AC-02 Verification

- [ ] CHK008 Are execution matrix requirements defined with explicit target OS runners (Linux and Windows) on Python 3.11 baseline and Python 3.12? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, AC-02, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK009 Are platform-specific edge cases (CRLF vs LF line endings and POSIX vs Windows path differences) addressed to prevent false positive CI failures? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## 5. Dependency Reproducibility & Determinism

- [ ] CHK010 Are pinned dependency version requirements (`==`) specified for all CI tools to guarantee deterministic, reproducible installation across environments? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Plan §Technical Context]

## 6. Integration Protection & Evidence Separation

- [ ] CHK011 Is the distinction between workflow execution failure (`exit code != 0`) and remote branch protection rule enforcement on GitHub explicitly documented? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Plan §Constraints]
- [ ] CHK012 Are required evidences explicitly classified into Evidence A (local validation), Evidence B (remote GitHub Actions run), and Evidence C (branch protection governance)? [Traceability, Plan §Technical Context, Quickstart §4]

---

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewer confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied in the specification and plan.
- All items start unchecked (`[ ]`) per the reviewer ownership model.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and does not modify markers.
